sentences.text:
1. The petitioner is aggrieved by the unilateral action of the respondent authority in trying to dispossess the petitioner and demolish the petitioner's property admeasuring 95.55 square yards,
situated at Gurunanak Colony, Vijayawada.

sentences.text: It is submitted that the 2nd respondent had earlier made similar attempts to dispossess the petitioner and others under the guise of road widening.

At that point of time, the petitioner and other similarly situated property owners approached this Court by filing WP.No.16899 of 2016 and batch, and this Court disposed of said writ petitions, making it clear to the respondent authorities to negotiate with the stakeholders for road widening.

In the event the landowners were not willing to accept the offer in pursuance of G.O.Ms.Nos.168 or 119, the 2nd respondent was directed to follow the procedure established under law for demolishing structures or dispossessing the occupants.
Insofar as the petitioners therein were assigned plots, liberty was granted to the respondents to negotiate for allotment of alternate plot/accommodation.

3. It is submitted that after a lapse of more than seven years, the 2nd respondent has once again initiated the process of taking over the petitioner's property and has also dumped material for laying road.
This Court, by order dated 09.10.2025, directed the respondent authority not to dispossess the petitioner without following due process of law.

4. The 2nd respondent has filed a counter, and the learned Standing Counsel appearing for the 2nd respondent submitted that the petitioner was invited to participate in negotiations for taking over the petitioner's property for the purpose of road widening in terms of the Master Plan.
It is submitted that the petitioner did not attend the negotiations and instead chose to file the present writ petition.

It is further submitted that several parties whose properties are situated in the same locality have expressed their consent for accepting TDR bonds in the ratio 1:4 in terms of G.O.Ms.No.119 and have cooperated with the road widening process.

It is submitted that the petitioner is insisting on payment of compensation instead of accepting TDR bonds, contending that the petitioner has to discharge a loan obtained against the said property from bankers.

5. The learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner is refusing to cooperate with the proposed road widening and that, under the guise of non-cooperation; the respondent authorities are trying to dispossess the petitioner from the property.

The petitioner has filed a rejoinder to the counter and has placed on record the loan sanction order issued by HDFC Bank, showing that the petitioner obtained a loan of Rs.1,50,00,00/- by mortgaging the said property.

It is submitted that if the respondent authority is permitted to take over the property without paying the compensation,
the petitioner would be left remediless and would be treated as a defaulter.
6. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Standing Counsel for the respondent authority.
Perused the material on record.
7. It is not in dispute that the respondents require the petitioner's property for the purpose of road widening.
It is also admitted that the petitioner was called upon to participate in negotiations, on par with other landlords whose properties are affected by the road widening process.

8. Considering the submissions that the petitioner is being compelled to participate in negotiations and accept TDR bonds instead of monetary compensation is concerned, the respondents are required to follow Section 146 of the A.P. Municipal Corporation Act, 1955, which deals with the acquisition of immovable property by agreement.

In the event the petitioner and the 2nd respondent Surapaneni Vijaya Nageswara Rao vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh And Others on 30 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68805297/
2 are unable to arrive at a consensus, the only option left to the 2nd respondent would be to invoke Section 147 of the A.P. Municipal Corporation Act, 1955, and proceed to acquire the property under the provisions of the Rights to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (Act 30 of 2013).

9. With the above observations, the present writ petition is disposed off, making it clear that the 2nd respondent shall follow Section 146 of the A.P. Municipal Corporation Act, 1955, and in the event of failure to arrive at an agreement, the 2nd respondent shall invoke the provisions of Section 147 of the A.P. Municipal Corporation Act, 1955, read with the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.
